caption:
StarCraft is coming back as an open-world shooter, but not until 2030.

Blizzard has officially revealed a new StarCraft game, described as a "story-driven open-world shooter." This marks the first new StarCraft title in over a decade, with the last release being the remaster of the original in 2017 and StarCraft 2 in 2010.

The game, simply titled "StarCraft," was announced with a cinematic trailer at BlizzCon 2026. Blizzard stated, "it's about damn time" for a new entry in the beloved real-time strategy franchise.

However, players will need to exercise patience, as the game is slated for release in spring 2030. This long development window means significant changes could occur between now and its launch.

Rumors of a StarCraft shooter have circulated for years, with several projects reportedly canceled during development. The last known attempt was discussed in 2024, highlighting the franchise's long-awaited transition into a new genre.

Source: Engadget, The Verge
